### Electron Version

from 30.0 to 39.2

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Both 10 and 11

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

29

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

In https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/41514/commits/8b4a97c230699296aa9223b33d59ce29e5523d33 (via https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/41514), the behavior of `app.getGpuInfo('complete')` changed from _**loading once and returning cached result**_ to _**requesting the latest GPU info every time**_.

This behavior change caused issues for code that depended on the previous caching behavior.

### Actual Behavior

This change was not mentioned in [Electron 30 release notes](https://www.electronjs.org/blog/electron-30-0). 😢 

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

Should this change be documented in the release notes, or only reflected in the latest API documentation?

nodes.title: Handling Relative Paths for Local File Loading via Custom Protocol after registerFileProtocol Deprecation
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

I am encountering an issue when attempting to load local files, particularly an index.html file, within an <iframe> using a custom protocol registered via protocol.handle.

The context is the upcoming deprecation of protocol.registerFileProtocol(), prompting migration to protocol.handle().

#### Problem

When a custom scheme is handled with protocol.handle, it is treated as a network request. This behavior prevents the resolution of relative paths within the loaded file, which is crucial for handling static assets.

#### Example:

A custom scheme is used to load an HTML file: <iframe src="custom://contents/index.html"></iframe>

The index.html file attempts to load a resource using a relative path: <video src="./assets/sample.mp4"></video>

The Electron/Chromium networking stack resolves the resource URL incorrectly as: custom://contents/index.html/assets/sample.mp4

This resolution logic mimics a standard server hosting environment where the path is appended, which is unsuitable for local file paths where the parent directory structure should be preserved.

Current Workarounds & Concerns
Using the file:// Protocol: Loading assets directly via file:// would resolve relative paths correctly, but this often requires setting webSecurity: false in the webPreferences of the BrowserWindow.

Web Security Risk: Disabling webSecurity poses significant security risks, especially in contexts where arbitrary or untrusted content might be loaded.

#### Question / Feature Request

How can a custom scheme registered with protocol.handle be configured to resolve relative paths and treat the request as a local file protocol (file:// behavior) for nested resources, without compromising security by globally disabling webSecurity?

A mechanism to properly handle the base URL and relative path resolution for assets served from the local file system using protocol.handle is urgently needed before registerFileProtocol is fully deprecated.

### Proposed Solution

A parameter (e.g., type: 'network' | 'file') should be added to the handler options.

### Alternatives Considered

or other method?..

### Additional Information

### Debugging Observation: FFmpegDecodeError on Second Playback

I attempted a manual resolution process within the iframe context to force relative path resolution using fs.isFile() checks.

However, a new issue arose specifically with video files:

The video file plays correctly for the first time, completing 100% of the playback.

Upon the second attempt to play the same video (triggering another request in the DevTools Network tab), an FFmpegDecodeError occurs.

### Observations:

I observed that the second request for the video file completes very quickly in the network tab.

No corresponding log for the second request appears within my protocol.handle() handler, suggesting the request might be intercepted or handled before reaching my custom logic.

This behavior leads me to suspect it may be an issue related to caching or an internal Chromium mechanism when handling media files served via a custom protocol.

nodes.title: Wrong user agent when changing Windows ProductName using rcedit
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

39.2.3

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 10 Pro 19045.2965

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

36.6.0 (broken in v36.7.0)

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

Electron is detected as a Chrome-based browser.

### Actual Behavior

Electron is detected as a Safari-based browser.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

When changing the "ProductName" of electron.exe using [rcedit](https://github.com/electron/rcedit):
```ps1
rcedit-x64.exe electron.exe --set-version-string ProductName Foo
```

The user-agent changes from something like
```
Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/142.0.7444.175 Electron/39.2.3 Safari/537.36
```
to
```
Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Foo/39.2.3 Safari/537.36
```

As you can see both the `Chrome` and `Electron` versions are removed, which means user-agent-based browser detections thinks the browser is a Safari browser (https://bowser-js.github.io/bowser-online/).

This seems to have changed from v36.6.0 to v36.7.0:

### Problem Description

Applications sandboxed behind Flatpak or other means do not always have access to read the configuration, thus they are stuck with garbage 1990s features like "gtk-enable-primary-paste" using the middle button to paste being enabled even when it's disabled by the user through their settings.

Currently Slack and Discord cannot resolve this issue with their software, as they are limited by Electron's capabilities.

### Proposed Solution

Offer a generic solution for any GTK setting to be overridden through the metadata or programmatically at runtime. The second option would be more useful to application developers

### Alternatives Considered

A single option for toggling that particular GTK setting would be possible, but a waste of effort if app developers want access to more of the settings.

_No response_

nodes.title: Allow clicking through areas of a webContentView
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

We want to build an Electron app that offers external web content (inside a webContentView) in a section of a BaseWindow. Above that, we want to offer our custom UI that surrounds the web app content.

### Proposed Solution

There should be a mechanism inside webContentView that allows the dev to define that clicks on a certain area are pass-through to the next lower view. This way, we can keep the UI on top of everything with native performance of the actual web content.

One way to implement the check: A CSS-Class similar to "app-region: drag" that allows to define if an area of the app catches the whole event or let's the event pass through to the next layer. Alternatively (though inconsistent with existing similar functions), we could offer some function in the main process API for WebContentsView to add a "pass-through" area.

Technically, we could extend the respective functions of the Chromium "View" base class to make extra checks for these areas (and then return "no hit" if such an area is the one clicked).

### Alternatives Considered

There is no functionality in Electron to accommodate this use case. Existing hacks like forwarding mouseEvents to other webContentViews come with limitations and edge-cases, and stacking multiple windows with "setIgnoreMouseEvents" feels like the worst of all hacks.

### Additional Information

Pulled Electron just now and trying to implement this on my own. Ideally I can offer a PR to get this done quickly since we really need it.

nodes.title: Electron Bug Report: `require('electron')` Returns Executable Path Instead of API Objects on Windows
nodes.body:

- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

31.7.7 and 32.2.2

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

Under development. This is the first version

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

Se report under additional Information

### Actual Behavior

Se report under additional Information

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

# Electron Bug Report: `require('electron')` Returns Executable Path Instead of API Objects on Windows

## Summary

On Windows, when running Electron applications, `require('electron')` incorrectly resolves to the npm package's `node_modules/electron/index.js` which exports the path to the executable (`electron.exe`), instead of being intercepted by Electron's internal module loader to provide the Electron API objects (`app`, `BrowserWindow`, etc.).

This causes a critical failure where all Electron applications fail to start with:
```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'whenReady')
```

## Environment

- **OS**: Windows 10/11
- **Node.js**: v20.18.0 and v22.18.0 (tested both)
- **npm**: 10.9.3
- **Electron**: v31.7.7 and v39.2.2 (both affected)
- **Package Manager**: npm (also tested with bun v1.3.1, same issue)

## Expected Behavior

When `require('electron')` is called from within an Electron main process:

1. Electron's internal module loader (`c._load` in `node:electron/js2c/node_init`) should intercept the require call
2. Return the Electron API object containing `{ app, BrowserWindow, ipcMain, dialog, ... }`
3. Allow the application to start normally

## Actual Behavior

1. `require('electron')` resolves to `node_modules/electron/index.js`
2. That file returns the string path: `"C:\\path\\to\\node_modules\\electron\\dist\\electron.exe"`
3. Destructuring `const { app, BrowserWindow } = require('electron')` results in `undefined` values
4. Application crashes when trying to call `app.whenReady()`

## Reproduction

### Minimal Reproduction Repository

Project structure:
```
project/
├── package.json
├── electron/
│   └── main.cjs
└── node_modules/
    └── electron/
```

### Step 1: Create package.json
```json
{
  "name": "electron-bug-test",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "main": "electron/main.cjs",
  "scripts": {
    "start": "electron ."
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "electron": "^31.7.7"
  }
}
```

### Step 2: Create electron/main.cjs
```javascript
const { app, BrowserWindow } = require('electron');

console.log('Type of require("electron"):', typeof require('electron'));
console.log('Value:', require('electron'));
console.log('app:', app);
console.log('BrowserWindow:', BrowserWindow);

app.whenReady().then(() => {
  console.log('Electron started successfully');
});
```

### Step 3: Install and Run
```bash
npm install
npm start
```

### Expected Output:
```
Type of require("electron"): object
Value: [object Object]
app: [Function: app]
BrowserWindow: [Function: BrowserWindow]
Electron started successfully
```

### Actual Output:
```
Type of require("electron"): string
Value: C:\path\to\node_modules\electron\dist\electron.exe
app: undefined
BrowserWindow: undefined

C:\path\to\electron\main.cjs:7
app.whenReady().then(() => {
    ^

TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'whenReady')
    at Object.<anonymous> (C:\path\to\electron\main.cjs:7:5)
    at Module._compile (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1484:14)
    at Module._extensions..js (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1564:10)
    at Module.load (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1295:32)
    at Module._load (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1111:12)
    at c._load (node:electron/js2c/node_init:2:16955)
    at Function.executeUserEntryPoint [as runMain] (node:internal/modules/run_main:189:12)
    at node:internal/main/run_main_module:28:49
```

## Analysis

### What We Discovered

1. **Electron's Internal Loader DOES Fire**: The stack trace shows `at c._load (node:electron/js2c/node_init:2:16955)`, confirming that Electron's module interception system is being invoked.

2. **But It Doesn't Provide the Module**: Instead of providing the Electron APIs, the internal loader falls back to Node's standard module resolution, which finds `node_modules/electron/index.js`.

3. **The npm Package Returns the Path**: The `node_modules/electron/index.js` file by design exports the executable path (for CLI usage), not the API objects:
```javascript
// From node_modules/electron/index.js
module.exports = getElectronPath(); // Returns string path to electron.exe
```

### What We Tested

#### Test 1: Renaming node_modules/electron
When we temporarily renamed `node_modules/electron` to `node_modules/.electron-hidden`:

**Result**:
```
Error: Cannot find module 'electron'
Require stack:
- c:\path\to\electron\main.cjs
    at Module._resolveFilename (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1232:15)
    at Module._load (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1058:27)
    at c._load (node:electron/js2c/node_init:2:16955)  ← Electron loader fires!
```

This proves Electron's `c._load` IS being called, but it throws `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` instead of providing the internal APIs.

#### Test 2: Custom Module Resolution Override
We attempted to override `Module._resolveFilename` to force MODULE_NOT_FOUND for the electron package:

```javascript
const Module = require('module');
const originalResolveFilename = Module._resolveFilename;

Module._resolveFilename = function(request, parent, isMain, options) {
  if (request === 'electron') {
    const error = new Error(`Cannot find module 'electron'`);
    error.code = 'MODULE_NOT_FOUND';
    throw error;
  }
  return originalResolveFilename.call(this, request, parent, isMain, options);
};

const electron = require('electron'); // Still returns string!
```

**Result**: Same issue - returns the executable path string.

#### Test 3: Downgrading Node.js
- **Node v20.18.0**: Same issue
- **Node v22.18.0**: Same issue

#### Test 4: Different Electron Versions
- **Electron v31.7.7**: Affected
- **Electron v39.2.2**: Affected

## Root Cause Hypothesis

Based on our testing, we believe the issue is:

1. Electron's internal module loader (`c._load`) is properly hooked into Node's module system
2. However, it's not registering `'electron'` as an internal module that it should provide
3. When the lookup fails internally, it falls back to standard Node.js module resolution
4. Node finds `node_modules/electron/index.js` and returns its export (the path string)

This suggests that **Electron's internal module registration is not working correctly** on this Windows configuration.

## Attempted Workarounds

### Workaround 1: Custom Electron Loader Module ❌
Created a wrapper module that attempts to force Electron's internal loader. Failed because the internal loader doesn't provide the module.

### Workaround 2: Runtime Directory Renaming ❌
Attempted to temporarily rename `node_modules/electron` at runtime to force MODULE_NOT_FOUND. Failed due to:
- File permissions (EPERM errors)
- Electron's loader still doesn't provide APIs even when npm package is missing

### Workaround 3: Module Cache Manipulation ❌
Tried deleting from `require.cache` and various resolution overrides. None successful.

## System-Specific Details

This bug appears to be **Windows-specific** and possibly related to:
- Node.js internal module loading changes in v20+
- Windows file system casing or path resolution
- Electron's module bootstrap sequence on Windows
- Interaction between Electron's ASAR handling and module resolution

## Impact

This is a **critical blocker** that prevents:
- Any Electron application from starting on affected systems
- Development of Electron applications
- Using any npm packages that depend on Electron APIs

## Additional Information

### Debug Output from Working System (Expected)
On systems where this works correctly:
```javascript
console.log(typeof require('electron')); // "object"
console.log(require('electron').app);    // [Function: app]
```

### Debug Output from Affected System (Actual)
```javascript
console.log(typeof require('electron')); // "string"
console.log(require('electron'));        // "C:\\...\\electron.exe"
console.log(require('electron').app);    // undefined
```

### Environment Variables
No unusual environment variables are set:
- `NODE_PATH`: Not set
- `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE`: Not set
- `ELECTRON_NO_ASAR`: Not set (also tested with it set to '1', same issue)

## Request for Help

We've exhausted all known workarounds. This appears to be a fundamental issue with how Electron's internal module system is initialized or registered on Windows.

**Questions for Electron Team:**
1. Is there a known issue with Electron's internal module loader on Windows + Node v20+?
2. Are there any environment variables or configuration that affects module registration?
3. Could this be related to how Electron detects it's running in Electron vs Node mode?
4. Is there diagnostic output we can enable to see what Electron's internal loader is doing?

## Files for Reference

### node_modules/electron/index.js
```javascript
const fs = require('fs');
const path = require('path');

const pathFile = path.join(__dirname, 'path.txt');

function getElectronPath () {
  let executablePath;
  if (fs.existsSync(pathFile)) {
    executablePath = fs.readFileSync(pathFile, 'utf-8');
  }
  if (process.env.ELECTRON_OVERRIDE_DIST_PATH) {
    return path.join(process.env.ELECTRON_OVERRIDE_DIST_PATH, executablePath || 'electron');
  }
  if (executablePath) {
    return path.join(__dirname, 'dist', executablePath);
  } else {
    throw new Error('Electron failed to install correctly, please delete node_modules/electron and try installing again');
  }
}

module.exports = getElectronPath(); // ← This is what's being returned!
```

### node_modules/electron/path.txt
```
electron.exe
```

## Related Issues

- Electron Issue #... (if similar issues exist)
- Node.js Issue #... (if related to Node module changes)

## Potential Fix Direction

Based on our analysis, a potential fix might involve:

1. Ensuring Electron's internal `ModuleWrap` or native module system properly registers the 'electron' module before Node's standard resolution kicks in
2. Investigating why `c._load` fires but doesn't provide the module on Windows
3. Possibly adding more aggressive interception of 'electron' requires before falling back to file system lookup

---

**Thank you for investigating this critical issue. Happy to provide any additional information or testing.**

**Reported by**: JEBL-Prosjekter Development Team
**Date**: 2025-11-18
**Contact**: Birger Lundgård

Windows ### Operating System Version Windows 10 20H2 ### What arch are you using? x64 ### Last Known Working Electron version _No response_ ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? I don't know how to test ### Expected Behavior Video should have both image and sound, regardless of whether there is a transparent window block out it or not. ### Actual Behavior - When the transparent window completely block out the window playing video, the image of the video will not be displayed, only the sound. - When the transparent window only partially block out the window playing video, the image of the video will be displayed normally. - When the transparent window completely block out a Google Chrome window playing video, the image will not be displayed either. ### Testcase Gist URL https://gist.github.com/zhujin917/93a78ff2ad3ccd702332a9cb1c212257 ### Additional Information It seems like Chromium is attempting to conserve performance, but it forgot to check whether the window above is transparent. I'm not sure if this is a Chromium or Electron issue, but I wish this can be fixed by Electron team, as Google Chrome will not create a transparent window.

nodes.title: Electron Module Initialization Failure on macOS 15.6.1
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

39.2.2 (also tested with 28.3.3, 33.0.0)

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS 15.6.1 (24G90) - Sequoia

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

Unknown (issue appears to be macOS-specific)

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

When launching an Electron application, the `require('electron')` statement should return the Electron API object with properties such as `app`, `BrowserWindow`, etc. The `process.type` property should be set to either `'browser'` or `'renderer'` depending on the process context.

### Actual Behavior

On macOS 15.6.1, Electron's JavaScript bootstrap layer fails to initialize. This results in:

1. `process.type` returning `undefined` instead of `'browser'` or `'renderer'`
2. `require('electron')` returning a string (file path) instead of the Electron API object
3. All Electron applications failing to launch with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined`

## To Reproduce

### Minimal Reproduction

**Step 1:** Create a minimal test file (`test-electron-minimal.js`):

```javascript
// Absolute minimal Electron test
console.log('=== Electron Module Load Test ===');
console.log('process.type:', process.type);
console.log('process.versions.electron:', process.versions.electron);

try {
  const electron = require('electron');
  console.log('require("electron") type:', typeof electron);
  console.log('require("electron") value:', electron);

  if (typeof electron === 'object' && electron !== null) {
    console.log('Keys:', Object.keys(electron).slice(0, 10));
    console.log('app exists:', 'app' in electron);
    console.log('BrowserWindow exists:', 'BrowserWindow' in electron);
  }
} catch (error) {
  console.error('ERROR loading electron:', error);
}

console.log('=== Test Complete ===');

// If we're in an Electron context, try to use the app
if (typeof require('electron').app === 'object') {
  const { app } = require('electron');
  app.whenReady().then(() => {
    console.log('SUCCESS: App is ready!');
    app.quit();
  });
} else {
  console.log('FAILED: Electron API not available');
  process.exit(1);
}
```

**Step 2:** Run with Electron:

```bash
npx electron test-electron-minimal.js
```

**Expected Output:**

```
=== Electron Module Load Test ===
process.type: browser
process.versions.electron: 39.2.2
require("electron") type: object
Keys: [ 'app', 'BrowserWindow', ... ]
app exists: true
BrowserWindow exists: true
=== Test Complete ===
SUCCESS: App is ready!
```

**Actual Output (macOS 15.6.1):**

```
=== Electron Module Load Test ===
process.type: undefined
process.versions.electron: 39.2.2
require("electron") type: string
require("electron") value: /path/to/node_modules/electron/dist/Electron.app/Contents/MacOS/Electron
=== Test Complete ===
FAILED: Electron API not available
```

### Reproduction with Official Sample

The issue also reproduces with the official `electron-quick-start` repository:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/electron/electron-quick-start
cd electron-quick-start
npm install
npm start
```

**Result:** Same failure - application does not launch.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

## Additional Information

### Diagnostic Evidence

#### 1. Electron Framework Loads Successfully

Using `DYLD_PRINT_LIBRARIES=1`, we confirmed the Electron Framework binary loads correctly:

```
dyld[12345]: <...> /path/to/Electron.app/Contents/Frameworks/Electron Framework.framework/Electron Framework
```

#### 2. Electron Version Detected

The `process.versions.electron` property correctly shows `"39.2.2"`, indicating the Electron runtime is partially initialized.

#### 3. Module Resolution Returns Path String

The npm wrapper at `node_modules/electron/index.js` correctly exports the Electron binary path. However, Electron's require hook system (which should replace this path with the API object) never executes.

#### 4. Environment Variables

- `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE` is **not set** (ruling out issue #8200)
- No IDE-specific environment variables present (ruling out issue #27135)
- Clean terminal execution with no special environment

### System Configuration

```bash
$ sw_vers
ProductName:            macOS
ProductVersion:         15.6.1
BuildVersion:           24G90

$ uname -m
arm64

$ node --version
v20.11.0

$ npm --version
10.2.4
```

### Attempted Fixes (All Failed)

We systematically attempted all standard Electron troubleshooting steps:

1. **Removed quarantine flags:**

   ```bash
   xattr -cr node_modules/electron/dist/Electron.app
   ```

   Result: No effect

2. **Re-signed application bundle:**

   ```bash
   codesign --remove-signature node_modules/electron/dist/Electron.app
   codesign -s - --deep --force node_modules/electron/dist/Electron.app
   ```

   Result: No effect

3. **Purged Electron caches:**

   ```bash
   rm -rf ~/Library/Caches/com.github.Electron
   rm -rf ~/Library/Application\ Support/Electron
   ```

   Result: No effect

4. **Tested multiple Electron versions:**

   - Electron 28.3.3: Failed
   - Electron 33.0.0: Failed
   - Electron 39.2.2: Failed
     Result: All versions fail identically

5. **Tested official samples:**

   - electron-quick-start: Failed
     Result: Official repository also affected

6. **Direct binary execution:**

   ```bash
   ./node_modules/electron/dist/Electron.app/Contents/MacOS/Electron test-electron-minimal.js
   ```

   Result: Same failure

7. **Launched from Terminal (bypass LaunchServices):**
   Result: No effect

### Root Cause Analysis

The evidence points to a system-level issue in macOS 15.6.1 that prevents Electron's JavaScript bootstrap from executing:

1. **Framework loads:** The Electron Framework dylib loads successfully
2. **Native layer initializes:** `process.versions.electron` is set by native code
3. **Bootstrap fails:** The JavaScript layer that installs the `require('electron')` hook never executes
4. **Result:** `require('electron')` returns the npm wrapper's path string instead of the API object

This suggests macOS 15.6.1's dynamic linker (dyld) or security policy is preventing Electron's embedded Node.js from completing its initialization sequence.
